surfaces.part: glass shards and rusty scrap lying flat on the ground

answer.evidence: The object is a scatter of glass shards and a bent rusty scrap seen from above, 16 rows tall and up to 16 px wide. The column scans show only mixed colours (grey-blue glass, rust brown, dark outline, white highlights) with no front-edge line, eave shadow or ellipse. No vertical south face of 3 or more rows is drawn. It reads as a flat decal on the ground, which fits the flat kind.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny prop of about 10x9 source pixels on a flat dark grey backdrop. It is not a 4x3-tile ground patch like the grass and paving references, which fill their whole areas with continuous surface texture. Its 21 visible tones per tile are measured over a very small footprint and do not mean a whole tile carries that much information. The dark edge pixels are tinted (2% neutral), so the outline is not a plain black sticker line. The shards and the rust scrap have only about 3-4 lightness steps each and little grain or dot texture. Most of the intended ground area is empty, so it reads as a small sticker-like object rather than a textured ground surface. Next to the references it looks thinner and much less dense, and a careful artist would not accept it as a ground patch.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate on the board is a tiny object sprite of roughly 12x10 source pixels, not a 4x3-tile ground patch. It shows a rusty scrap and a few shards on a dark backdrop, with no continuous ground surface, so it can't be compared fairly with the grass and paving references. The piece reads as a small prop and doesn't deliver the required ground-patch coverage or texture. When in doubt, fail.
